purpose: This tool shows one relationship as a table and as a graph. You will learn to find the unit rate k, and to tell a proportional relationship from one that only grows, by checking a table and a line through the origin.

stops.title: Table and graph
stops.text: The top is a table: x in green, y in red, and a blue row showing k times x for your line. Below is the graph. Each yellow dot is one table column. In step 1, drag the ringed point at x = 1 up or down to aim the blue line.
stops.try: Drag the ringed point until the blue line goes through every dot.

stops.title: Situation
stops.text: Pick a story: tickets, recipes, walking, taxi, pool membership and more. Some are proportional and some are not. In the not-proportional ones, no line through the origin can hit every dot. Step 1 only.
stops.try: Choose Taxi ride and try to hit every dot. Why can you not?

stops.title: Unit rate k
stops.text: k is the cost of one thing, or the height of the line at x = 1. The slider and the ringed point do the same job. The panel tells you how many dots the line hits, and whether it is above or below.
stops.try: Move k until the readout says the line goes through every dot.

stops.title: The y over x row
stops.text: This adds a row to the table that divides y by x in each column. If every column gives the same number, that number is k, and the relationship is proportional. Different numbers mean it is not.
stops.try: Turn it on and compare the row for Movie tickets and Taxi ride.

stops.title: Connect and extend
stops.text: This joins the dots with a line and runs it back to x = 0. A proportional line goes through the origin (0, 0). A line that crosses the y axis higher up is not proportional. The next switch draws a triangle to show k.
stops.try: Turn it on and see where the line meets the y axis.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 sets k by hand. Step 2 uses k to fill in a missing table entry. Step 3 asks if a table, graph or story is proportional. Step 4 matches words, table, graph and equation. Next question moves on inside a step.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Two questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 1 and ask students to fix the line, then switch to Taxi ride. Many say the taxi is proportional because it grows. Ask what it costs to ride 0 miles. In step 3, ask for the test in words before anyone answers: the same y divided by x, and through the origin.
